title: Startup ecosystems and founder networks
note: A startup being new, funded or AI-focused does not automatically mean it needs these services.
objective: Discover startups and founders who may need practical AI implementation, workflow automation, integrations or technical delivery support.
sources: Public demo-day and pitch-event participant lists
Startup project briefs and partnership announcements
access_rules: Use public and permitted information only.
Verify each opportunity through its original source whenever possible.
target_profiles: SaaS businesses integrating AI into workflows
Early-stage products requiring an MVP or integration prototype
Startups handling customer inquiries or lead intake
Companies seeking CRM, messaging or operational integrations
AI products needing RAG or knowledge retrieval
Startups looking for automation implementation partners
Agencies and startups seeking flexible technical delivery capacity
target_profile_rule: These are discovery categories, not proof of need.

A.name: Explicit requirement
examples: A founder asks for an automation developer
A startup publishes a relevant contractor or implementation request
A company describes a specific integration project
A founder requests help implementing an AI assistant or workflow
A startup seeks a technical partner for a clearly defined deliverable

B.name: Specific product or workflow evidence
examples: A product publicly documents a particular integration gap
A company describes a recurring process that matches a supported service
A startup publicly explains a technical implementation challenge
A founder discusses a project and invites relevant technical assistance

C.name: General startup activity
examples: A startup participates in an accelerator
A company describes itself as AI-powered
A startup is expanding its team without a relevant technical requirement
C.caveat: May justify monitoring or further research, but not claims of buying intent.

tier_mapping.note: Tier C alone is not admitted as a qualified lead.

research_workflow: Verify the company's name, official domain and product.
Review the public product description and relevant documentation.
Identify a specific requirement or workflow opportunity.
Identify the founder or relevant technical/operations decision-maker, if verified.
Determine whether the startup is seeking a contractor, employee, co-founder or partner.
Match the requirement to one supported service.
Assess project scope and commercial suitability.
assumption_rule: Do not assume a startup wants a freelancer simply because it has a technical roadmap.

questions: Is the startup actively seeking implementation help?
Is the required work within actual capabilities?
Is the scope suitable for a small pilot or project?
Is there a legitimate contact channel?
Are payment or funding assumptions supported by evidence?
commercial_qualification.funding_rule: Funding announcements do not establish an available budget. Do not invent funding amounts, runway, purchasing authority or urgency.
commercial_qualification.employment_rule: Distinguish employee vacancies from contractor opportunities. If the startup is recruiting only a full-time employee, do not misrepresent a service offer as a job application.

portfolio_matching.rule: Use only relevant examples and do not claim unverified production metrics or commercial outcomes.

implementation_signal.question: How strong is the implementation signal?

service_fit.question: Does the requirement match a deliverable service?

contractor_suitability.question: Is a contractor or project engagement plausible?

decision_maker_contactability.question: Is there a route to a verified decision-maker and a specific outreach reason?

scoring.gate: A high score means the lead deserves further investigation, not that it has buying intent. Do not assign a high implementation-signal score solely because a startup is AI-focused, recently launched or funded.

missing_value_rule: Use unknown or null when information is unavailable.

must: Reference a specific product, requirement or founder statement
Offer one relevant implementation service or a narrowly scoped pilot
Explain why demonstrated capabilities match the stated requirement
must_not: Pitch every startup an AI chatbot
Assume a funding announcement means a startup can afford the service
Claim to have evaluated private infrastructure
Pretend to be an investor, accelerator representative or job applicant
Promise product-market fit, revenue growth or unverified performance improvements
outreach_strategy.no_trigger_rule: If there is no credible trigger, retain the startup as a low-priority prospect or exclude it.

operating_principle: Prioritize startups with verifiable requirements and a plausible path to a paid technical engagement, not startups merely because they are new, funded or interested in AI.

quantity_policy.rule: No numeric limit. Return every qualified startup and no unqualified ones.
